Risk Statement: One client's documents or graph entries being retrieved into an answer for another client, through a shared index or a mis-tagged document, resulting in disclosure of confidential bank information and breach of contract.
Existing Controls: One knowledge base and graph per client by design; analyst sign-off on every answer
Treatment Actions: Enforce client separation at retrieval with attribute-based access (client tag on every chunk, checked against the requester); plant canary documents per client and fail the release if any appears in another client's answer; quarterly cross-client retrieval test

Risk Statement: An answer containing a claim its cited source does not support being approved by an analyst who reviews at volume, resulting in a client giving its regulator or auditor an incorrect statement of control.
Existing Controls: Every claim must carry a citation; analyst sign-off required before release
Treatment Actions: Automated check that each claim's citation contains supporting text, blocking release on failure; seeded known-bad answers in the review queue to measure reviewer catch rate; monitor override and edit rates (near-zero edits flags rubber-stamping); record what the reviewer saw, changed and why
EU AI Act: Art. 14 principles applied voluntarily (system not high-risk; see MIC-CLS-001)

Risk Statement: Instructions hidden in a log line, ticket or runbook read by an operations agent steering its triage, because guardrails screen user input and final answers but not tool input and output, resulting in a misleading triage that an engineer acts on during an incident.
Existing Controls: Read-only tools only in v1 (MIC-DEC-003); human engineer executes every fix through the client's change process
Treatment Actions: Treat all tool output as data: strip and flag instruction-like content before it reaches the model; show the engineer the raw evidence behind each triage step; red-team the agents with injected log lines before each release

Risk Statement: A new agent tool with write access, or a wider data scope, being added to an operations agent without AI Risk Committee approval, resulting in an agent able to change a client's production systems.
Existing Controls: Cedar policies deny by default; AI Risk Committee approves every new agent and model change
Treatment Actions: Pipeline check that blocks deployment of any tool or policy change not listed as approved in the AI system inventory (MIC-INV-001); write-capable tools rejected in v1 regardless of approval; monthly diff of deployed tools against the inventory

Risk Statement: EU or Indian client content being processed outside its jurisdiction through a cross-region inference option or a misconfigured service, resulting in breach of the residency commitments in client contracts and unlawful transfer.
Existing Controls: Residency stated at jurisdiction level (MIC-DEC-010); Frankfurt and Mumbai only; Hyderabad reserved
Treatment Actions: IAM deny on all regions outside each jurisdiction's allowed set; in-region model endpoints only, global or cross-region inference profiles blocked by policy; AWS Config rule alerting on resources created outside allowed regions

Risk Statement: Sextant depending on a single model provider and platform for every AI service, so a supplier restriction, outage or terms change stops delivery to all five clients. Partly realised: model invocation has been blocked on the lab account since September (F-06).
Existing Controls: Model layer designed on Amazon Bedrock; lab proceeds without live invocation (MIC-DEC-012)
Treatment Actions: Model-agnostic interface so a second provider can be switched in without redesign; documented exit plan and tested fallback for each AI service; supplier review of model terms (training on inputs, retention, region) each quarter

Risk Statement: Rheinmark Bank and Veluwe Payments not receiving complete and current information on Sextant's ICT subcontractors, because subcontracting changes are not tracked, resulting in the banks' DORA registers of information being wrong and a contract breach.
Existing Controls: DORA Article 30 obligations recorded in client contracts (MIC-DEC-001)
Treatment Actions: Maintain a subcontractor register per client service; notify the EU clients before any material subcontracting change; annual exit-plan test for each critical function

Risk Statement: Engineers pasting client logs, tickets or documents into personal AI tools to speed up work, resulting in client confidential and personal data leaving Meridian's control.
Existing Controls: Group acceptable use policy; secure client bays
Treatment Actions: AI use and governance policy with approved tools only (MIC-POL-001); block uploads to unapproved AI services from client bays and managed devices; AI literacy training with acknowledgement on joining and yearly; monthly discovery of AI service use from proxy logs

Risk Statement: Long-lived access keys or standing administrator access to the Sextant AWS environment being stolen or misused, resulting in access to every client's content.
Existing Controls: No access keys; human access through aws login with MFA (MIC-DEC-008); root used only for root-only tasks and reconciled against CloudTrail
Treatment Actions: Time-limited elevation for administrator roles; alert on any root sign-in or access-key creation; quarterly access review

Risk Statement: Logs or evidence files being altered or deleted after collection, resulting in audit evidence that a client's auditor cannot rely on.
Existing Controls: Evidence fingerprinted with SHA-256 and kept byte-exact in the repository
Treatment Actions: Write evidence to an S3 bucket with Object Lock (compliance mode) and versioning; record fingerprints at collection; keep a 180-day log copy in Mumbai

Risk Statement: Client staff and auditors not being told that answers and triages are drafted by AI, resulting in loss of trust and a gap against transparency obligations.
Existing Controls: Analyst or engineer approval recorded on each output
Treatment Actions: Label every output as AI-drafted and human-approved, naming the approver; describe the AI role in each client contract
